item.text:
**Overall:** mostly no. I found evidence of a generally less coercive information environment than under Bolsonaro, plus some transparency and unblocking moves. The main caveats are targeted anti-disinformation actions, platform pressure, and one major court-enforced platform block, but I found no solid evidence of internet shutdowns or a Lula-led surveillance campaign to suppress opposition.

- [Onde posso acessar discursos e falas do presidente Lula?](https://www.gov.br/secom/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/perguntas-frequentes/onde-posso-acessar-discurso-e) - Secretaria de Comunicação Social - 2024-03-21 - The government directed the public to official transcripts, audio, and video archives for Lula’s speeches, which is a transparency measure rather than secrecy or propaganda. Question IDs: 4B.9, 4B.6.

- [Brazil | World Report 2024](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/brazil) - Human Rights Watch - 2024-01-11 - HRW said Lula’s government unblocked more than 3,000 social-media users previously blocked from interacting with institutional accounts under Bolsonaro, which is a concrete reversal of prior restrictions. Question IDs: 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5.

- [Brazil: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/brazil/freedom-world/2024) - Freedom House - 2024 - Freedom House described Brazil’s media environment as vibrant and competitive, and said the Lula administration did not keep Bolsonaro-era monitoring of public servants for criticism. Question IDs: 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5.

- [Brazil | Freedom on the Net 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/brazil/freedom-net/2024) - Freedom House - 2024 - Freedom House said online journalists and users generally faced a somewhat less restrictive environment under Lula than under Bolsonaro, though legal threats and harassment still existed. Question IDs: 4B.9, 4B.6.

- [Digital News Report 2024: Brazil](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/brazil) - Reuters Institute - 2024-06-17 - Reuters Institute said the “fake news” bill was eventually abandoned and that mainstream outlets remained trusted, which supports a relatively open information environment despite polarization. Question IDs: 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5.

- [Em 2024, jornalistas sofreram uma agressão a cada 2 dias e meio no Brasil, aponta relatório da Fenaj](https://www.abi.org.br/em-2024-jornalistas-sofreram-uma-agressao-a-cada-2-dias-e-meio-no-brasil-aponta-relatorio-da-fenaj/) - ABI / FENAJ - 2024-05-20 - FENAJ reported 144 attacks on journalists in 2024, down from 181 in 2023, which suggests improvement but still a serious harassment problem. Question IDs: 4B.9, 4B.6.

- [YouTube retira do ar desinformação sobre estado de saúde do presidente da República](https://www.gov.br/agu/pt-br/comunicacao/noticias/youtube-retira-do-ar-desinformacao-sobre-estado-de-saude-do-presidente-da-republica/) - Advocacia-Geral da União - 2024-12-16 - The government formally notified YouTube to remove videos spreading false claims about Lula’s health; this is the clearest counterevidence because it shows active state pressure on information flow, though framed as anti-disinformation rather than direct censorship of legitimate opposition speech. Question IDs: 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5.

- [Digital News Report 2024: Brazil](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/brazil) - Reuters Institute - 2024-06-17 - Reuters Institute said the justice minister threatened hourly fines when Google opposed the government’s platform bill, which is the main caveat on administrative pressure over the online sphere. Question IDs: 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5.

- [X has been blocked in Brazil. Does it matter for journalism?](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/news/x-has-been-blocked-brazil-does-it-matter-journalism) - Reuters Institute - 2024-09-16 - Brazil’s Supreme Court blocked X after the platform refused legal orders; journalists split on whether this was lawful enforcement or a speech problem. This is the strongest institutional caveat, but it is not clear Lula himself directed it. Question IDs: 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5.

Search gap: I found no credible 2024 evidence of Lula ordering internet shutdowns or building a broad surveillance system against opposition. The negative evidence is narrower: selective content takedowns, pressure around misinformation rules, and a court-driven platform block.
